deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This page is a draft opening of Riemann's 1860 memoir 'Über die Fortpflanzung ebener Luftwellen von endlicher Schwingungsweite'. The left column works out the thermodynamic pressure-density law. The right column searches for the Riemann (resolvent) function of the linear characteristic equation obtained on the previous page by the hodograph method.

A. TITLE AND INTRODUCTION. The heading reads 'Über die Fortpflanzung von Luftschwingungen (...) von B. Riemann'. The text says the differential equations of gas motion have long been known, but they have been integrated almost only when the pressure differences are infinitely small.

B. LEFT COLUMN: ADIABATIC LAW AND SPECIFIC HEATS.
1. Gas law. He writes p = ρτ (density times absolute temperature, constant absorbed). Hence log p = log ρ + log τ + const, so ∂log τ/∂log p = 1 and ∂log τ/∂log ρ = -1.
2. Heat absorbed. The heat is K (∂τ/∂ρ) dρ + V (∂τ/∂p) dp, where K is the specific heat at constant pressure and V at constant volume. He first wrote τ(K dlog ρ + V dlog p), with the wrong sign. He then corrected it to τ(V dlog p - K dlog ρ).
3. Adiabatic condition. Zero heat gives dlog p = (K/V) dlog ρ. With k = K/V constant (Poisson), this gives p ∝ ρ^k. The numbers 1.421 and 1.410 are candidate values of k.
4. Mayer's hypothesis. The mechanical equivalent of the excess heat equals the external work: A τ (K - V) dlog v = p dv, with v = 1/ρ. Hence K - V = pv/(Aτ).
5. Value of A. The figure 423.55 is the mechanical equivalent of heat in kilogram-metres per kilocalorie. It is exactly Joule's 772 ft·lbf/(lb·°F) converted: 772 × 0.3048 × 1.8 = 423.55.
6. Lower left, the same in v. He writes log p + log v = log T + const and K (∂T/∂v) dv + V (∂T/∂p) dp = T(K dlog v + V dlog p). This is the version that appears in the fair copy on the next page.

C. RIGHT COLUMN: ANSATZ FOR THE RIEMANN FUNCTION.
The equation from the previous page has the form w_pq = λ(p+q) w, with p, q the characteristic (Riemann-invariant) variables, σ = p+q and σ' = p'+q'. Riemann tries a similarity solution w = f(z), with z = (p-p')(q-q') ψ(σ).
1. First derivative: ∂w/∂p = f'·(q-q') ψ (1 + (p-p') ψ'/ψ).
2. Mixed derivative: ∂²w/∂p∂q = f'·[ψ + (σ-σ')ψ' + (p-p')(q-q')ψ''] + f''·(p-p')(q-q')[ψ² + (σ-σ')ψψ' + (p-p')(q-q')ψ'²]. He also writes the f'' term in the factored form f''(p-p')(q-q')ψ²(1+(p-p')ψ'/ψ)(1+(q-q')ψ'/ψ).
3. Conditions. For this to collapse to an ODE in z alone, he requires (i) ψ'²/ψ = β ψ'' and (ii) ψ(ψ + (σ-σ')ψ') = α ψ''.
4. Trial ψ = k(σ-γ)^β. Condition (i) holds automatically. Condition (ii) becomes k²(σ-γ)^{2β-1}((σ-γ) + β(σ-σ')) = α k β(β-1)(σ-γ)^{β-2}. This can hold identically in σ only if β = -1. Then it reduces to k(σ'-γ) = 2α.
5. Result of the β = -1 branch. ψ = k/(σ-γ), so z = k(p-p')(q-q')/(p+q-γ). This is (up to normalisation) the cross-ratio-type variable of the Euler–Poisson–Darboux equation. With it, w_pq = c(p+q-γ)^{-2} w reduces to a hypergeometric/Legendre ODE in z. This is the method of the published 1860 paper.
6. Abandoned branch. He also tries ψ' = kψ (exponential, so ψ'²/ψ = ψ''), which forces ψ(1 + k(σ-σ')) = k²α. That gives ψ = k²α/(1 + k(σ-σ')), with stated dlog ψ/dσ = k/(1 + k(σ-σ')). This branch is not followed further.
errors: Left column: the first expression τ(K dlog ρ + V dlog p) has the wrong sign on the K term; Riemann corrects it on the next line to τ(V dlog p - K dlog ρ).
Right column: the first attempt at the mixed derivative f''((p-p')ψ + ...)((q-q')ψ) is garbled; he crosses it out and rewrites the f' bracket.
The exponential branch is internally inconsistent: ψ' = kψ contradicts the derived ψ = k²α/(1 + k(σ-σ')), which is not exponential.
In that branch the logarithmic derivative has a sign slip: d log[k²α/(1 + k(σ-σ'))]/dσ = -k/(1 + k(σ-σ')), not +k/(1 + k(σ-σ')).
In condition (ii) with ψ = k(σ-γ)^β, α must depend on σ' (k(σ'-γ) = 2α). This is harmless, since σ' is a fixed parameter of the Riemann function.

results.what: Adiabatic law p ∝ ρ^k for an ideal gas with constant ratio of specific heats, derived from the heat differential
c_p - c_v = pv/(A T) from Mayer's hypothesis, with A = 423.55 kgm/kcal (Joule's value)
Similarity ansatz w = f((p-p')(q-q')ψ(p+q)) for the Riemann function of w_pq = λ(p+q)w; shows ψ ∝ 1/(σ-γ) is the power-law choice reducing the equation to an ODE in z
results.modern_name: Riemann function of the Euler–Poisson–Darboux equation (hypergeometric in a cross-ratio variable)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the published 1860 Luftwellen paper. The thermodynamics is standard and the Riemann-function ansatz is the known method of that paper. The only small new details are the trial-and-error search for ψ and the identification of 423.55 as Joule's converted value.

checkable.sympy: p,q,a,b=symbols('p q a b'); psi=Function('psi'); f=Function('f'); z=(p-a)*(q-b)*psi(p+q); s=p+q-a-b; P=psi(p+q); P1=Derivative(psi(p+q),p).doit().subs(Derivative(psi(p+q),p),diff(psi(p+q),p)); simplify(diff(f(z),p,q) - (Subs(diff(f(Symbol('x')),Symbol('x')),Symbol('x'),z).doit()*(P+s*diff(P,p)+(p-a)*(q-b)*diff(P,p,2)) + Subs(diff(f(Symbol('x')),Symbol('x'),2),Symbol('x'),z).doit()*(p-a)*(q-b)*(P**2+s*P*diff(P,p)+(p-a)*(q-b)*diff(P,p)**2)))
checkable.asserts: Mixed derivative of f((p-p')(q-q')ψ(p+q)) equals Riemann's f'[...] + f''(p-p')(q-q')[...] expression (expect 0)
With ψ = k/(σ-γ), ψ(ψ+(σ-σ')ψ')/ψ'' is independent of σ (equals k(σ'-γ)/2)
For a power ψ, ψ'^2/ψ divided by ψ'' is the constant β/(β-1)
Gives -k/(1+k(σ-σ')), showing the sign slip on the page
Joule's 772 ft-lbf per lb per °F equals 423.55 kg·m per kcal

checkable.sympy: p,rho,k,C=symbols('p rho k C',positive=True); simplify(diff(log(C*rho**k),rho)*rho - k)
checkable.asserts: p = Cρ^k satisfies dlog p = k dlog ρ (adiabatic)

The heat expression on the left is K(∂τ/∂ρ)dρ + V(∂τ/∂p)dp; the following line τ(Kdlogρ + Vdlogp) is corrected to τ(V dlog p - K dlog ρ).
The 'A' in Aτ(K-V) dlog v = p dv is the mechanical equivalent of heat (423.55); it is struck and rewritten but retained in K - V = pv/(Aτ).
The line ψ'²/ψ = βψ'' has a crossed-out continuation '= k²ψ(σ)'; the first line reads ψ(σ)(ψ(σ)+(σ-σ')ψ'(σ)) = ψ''(σ)α.
The title likely reads 'Über die Fortpflanzung von Luftschwingungen' with a parenthetical such as '(endlicher Schwingungsweite)'; uncertain.
